Market structure and trend

The basis for reading what structure price is moving in; trend, swing highs and lows, and when the structure changes.

  • What is a trend?

    • Market structure

    A trend is price moving mostly in one direction over a period of time.

  • Swing highs and swing lows

    • Market structure

    A swing high is a point where price stops rising and turns down, standing above the candles on either side.

  • Higher highs, higher lows, lower highs, lower lows

    • Market structure

    Each new swing high and low is labelled by comparing it with the previous one: higher high (HH), higher low (HL), lower high (LH) and lower low (LL).

  • When does a trend count as changed?

    • Market structure

    An uptrend counts as broken when price closes below the last important higher low.

  • Pullback or reversal?

    • Market structure

    A pullback is a temporary move against the trend that leaves the structure intact.

  • Trendlines and channels

    • Market structure

    A trendline is a sloping line drawn by joining the lows in an uptrend or the highs in a downtrend.

  • Ranges and consolidation

    • Market structure

    A range is price moving back and forth between two zones without a clear direction.
